{"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","Punchline":"Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.","Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

{"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","AcceptsFeedback":false,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.3.0.3","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":null,"DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]

- **The v1.0.4.318 automatic-cleanse change is back, now fenced so the cleanse scan can never hang or spin a frame.** Same cleanse behaviour as before the withdrawal: dispellable debuffs are graded by worth (movement- and action-locking debuffs cleanse first, damage-over-time debuffs cleanse while the healer can spare the cast, damage-taken amplifiers and resist downs never take one, doom always, the dead never), hostile objects can no longer resolve as cleanse candidates anywhere, and one debuff can never consume two casts. New in this build, the cleanse scan runs behind a frame guard: it pauses right after a plugin reload and right after any territory change (the two windows the withdrawn build ran into trouble in), can never re-enter itself, and if a single scan ever costs more than a frame the plugin logs the managed call stack at the slow point and stands the scan down for two seconds instead of repeating next tick.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.319 withdrawal build. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.319 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **The v1.0.4.318 automatic-cleanse change is withdrawn; cleanse behaviour is again exactly the v1.0.4.317 behaviour.** The change graded dispellable debuffs by worth, required friendly targets along the Esuna retargeting chain and held a second cleanse back while a first was still resolving, but a full game freeze was reported with the build present, the main thread spinning inside the plugin's own managed code, and the exact looping path could not be established from the captured evidence. The whole change comes out rather than leave a suspected hazard on the heal path: the retargeting chain, the worth checks and the double-cast window of v1.0.4.317 are restored as they were.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.318 testing build, which is withdrawn. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.318 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **Automatic cleanses (Esuna and Exuviation) now fire only when the debuff is worth the cast, and never twice for the same debuff.** Three defects fixed at one shared verdict. First, the Esuna retargeting chain could resolve a hostile target: a mob carrying its own dispel-flagged damage-over-time effect (for example Combust III on the mob the DoT was cast on) outranked the real party member, so grinding a FATE could spend global cooldowns casting Esuna at a mob. The chain now requires a friendly target at every step, and hostile objects can no longer resolve as cleanse candidates anywhere. Second, the heal-combo cleanse branch and the auto-rotation's party cleanse were two independent casters for the same debuff while the status list still showed a debuff that a cast already in flight was removing, so one debuff could consume two casts seconds apart. Every cleanse send now goes through one shared verdict that remembers a cleanse sent in the last few seconds and stands down until it resolves. Third, every dispellable status was treated as equally worth a cast. The verdict now grades them: movement- and action-locking debuffs cleanse first, because cleansing them is the dodge; damage-over-time debuffs cleanse while the healer is healthy enough to spare the cast; damage-taken amplifiers and resist downs that fall off on their own never take one. Under low health only a cleansing doom is still worth the cast, and a dead candidate is never targeted.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.317 (2026-10-21) [testing]
- **The Cast-Start Stillness setting is removed, together with the v1.0.4.316 testing build it shipped in.** That build held a fresh cast bar for a moment after movement stopped to keep the bar from being glued onto a dodge, but casting into a stop is normal cast mechanics, not a stuck slide-cast, so the hold answered a problem the game does not have. Cast-start movement behaviour is again exactly the v1.0.4.315 behaviour: moving always blocks a new cast start, instant casts and orbwalker-driven movement never block, and a stopped player casts immediately. The v1.0.4.315 FATE-grind spike skip is untouched. A settings file that still carries the old key loads unchanged; the key is ignored and disappears at the next save.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.316 testing build, which is withdrawn. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.315 (2026-10-20) [testing]
- **The FATE-grind spike skip now stays on.** The first testing build of the part-of-pack spike skip (v1.0.4.314) checked for spiked mobs through its own skip list: with a skip armed, the next check saw the spiked mobs already hidden, believed none were left and switched the skip off, so the spiked mob could be targeted again on alternating ticks. The check now reads the full pack every tick, the skip stays armed while a spiked mob lives, and a pack that decays to only spiked mobs takes the full stop as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.314 testing build. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.314 (2026-10-20) [testing]
- **The enemy-reflect stop no longer freezes a FATE grind over spikes on part of the pack.** While another plugin drives the rotation with FATE priority inside a FATE, a mob carrying a reflect or counter-stance status (Ice Spikes, Shock Spikes, Blaze Spikes, the Counter stances) no longer stops every press for the status's full duration: the rotation attacks the rest of the pack first and leaves the carrier alone. The full stop keeps everything it covered before - manual play, foray territories (Eureka's charged spikes kill), and a pack where every target reflects - and still targets the player and cancels casts there. Every job the grind drives had the same stall, not only Summoner.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.1.0.0","Changelog":"API15 finally","DalamudApiLevel":"15","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.

- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrucible","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.5","CategoryTags":["jobs","utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.11 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction now waits for the roster itself to stop changing.** The previous fix judged a settled roster by edit timestamps, but the roster AutoDuty builds is driven through the monster notebook, whose selection writes never register as edits — so the timestamp stayed at screen-open while the build was still adding picks, and the correction still fired mid-build, where AutoDuty's continuing build and its confirm passes removed the added rows. The correction is now due only once the selected roster has been unchanged for 1.5 seconds — what the plugin sees every frame — never on an empty roster, and it still re-arms after any later AutoDuty write. The screen log's roster needfix line now also carries the age of the last edit (`adedit=`), the roster's quiet time (`adstb=`) and the selected count (`flutes=`).

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrucible","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.5","CategoryTags":["jobs","utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.11 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction now waits for the roster itself to stop changing.** The previous fix judged a settled roster by edit timestamps, but the roster AutoDuty builds is driven through the monster notebook, whose selection writes never register as edits — so the timestamp stayed at screen-open while the build was still adding picks, and the correction still fired mid-build, where AutoDuty's continuing build and its confirm passes removed the added rows. The correction is now due only once the selected roster has been unchanged for 1.5 seconds — what the plugin sees every frame — never on an empty roster, and it still re-arms after any later AutoDuty write. The screen log's roster needfix line now also carries the age of the last edit (`adedit=`), the roster's quiet time (`adstb=`) and the selected count (`flutes=`).

{"Author":"croizat, dajoey","Name":"Lazy Fate Automation","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.0.3.7","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

v0.0.3.6 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The server info bar entry shows the boss FATE icon instead of the sword glyphs.** The same icon is used in every state; the bot's on/off state stays in the text (": On", ": Off" and the rest), exactly as before. No other entry is affected.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The click behavior, the confirming second click and everything else in the previous build are unchanged.

v0.0.3.5 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **Server info bar (Umbra) toggle for the FATE bot.** The plugin adds a "Lazy Fate Automation" entry to the game's server info bar, which Umbra renders as a button. It shows the bot state with the sibling entries' sword icon: On, Off, "(stopping)" while a soft stop is pending, or the live state such as "Paused (in instance)". Clicking it stops the bot (Ctrl+click waits for the current FATE to finish, like the window's soft stop); when stopped, the first click arms the start and a second click within 10 seconds confirms it, so a stray click cannot start the automation. Starting still requires a logged-in character, exactly like the Lazy Hub switch.
- New display setting "Show server info bar entry" (on by default) hides or shows the entry; it can also be hidden per-plugin in Umbra or under /xlsettings -> Server Info Bar.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The Lazy Hub quick controls, the snapshot endpoint and all other behavior are unchanged.

v0.0.3.4 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The currency-focus fallback setting now takes effect.** In the previous version both fallback options kept rotating the focused zones identically. Zone swaps now first pass through every focused zone; once a full pass finds no FATE to run, "Continue normally" (default) resumes the usual zone rotation (achievement-guided / same expansion), while "Idle in zone" stays put and waits for focused-currency FATEs instead of grinding other FATEs.
- Excluding every focused zone now falls back the same way instead of waiting in place.
- The fallback setting's in-game help describes the new behavior.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Lazy Fish Sitter","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.5.1","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

v0.1.2.0 (2026-09-05)

- SUPERSEDED BY v0.1.3.0 AND NEVER FISHED ON: the design premise below was wrong. It claimed the game forces standing on every hooked fish; it does not - if the character was sitting before the hook, the game re-seats automatically. Everything in this entry that follows from that premise (a /sit per stand episode) was removed in v0.1.3.0. Kept here for the record only.
- Re-sat after every cast and every catch, on the mistaken premise above: the unit was a "stand episode" (fishing start, or the fishing state machine passing through Hooking/ReleasingCatch/ConfirmingCollectable), and each episode got at most ONE /sit (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Arm` / `TrackTransitions`).
- Sent only when it believed the game would accept it: read `EventFramework.Instance()->EventHandlerModule.FishingEventHandler` (FFXIVClientStructs) and required `State` to be `PoleReady` or `LineInWater` for at least 1 s with `ChangingPosition` false. Counting `LineInWater` as acceptable was the second defect - that is exactly where the emote gets swallowed (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Proof the sit took: `FishingEventHandler.ChangingPosition` going true within 3 s of the send was logged as `game accepted our sit`, with a 3 s outcome line per send. This part was correct and is kept in v0.1.3.0 (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`).
- No detector-driven re-arm: a "not seated" read after a sit never triggered a re-send on its own (that is what yo-yoed v0.1.0.0). Also kept in v0.1.3.0, hardened (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Logged every posture/fishing state CHANGE at Information, rate-limited to 40 lines/min: Fishing flag, FishingState, ChangingPosition, CanFish, Character.Mode/ModeParam, EmoteController.EmoteId, GetPosture(), and the combined SEATED verdict (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`, `LogTransition`).
- A failing FFXIVClientStructs signature (EventFramework or GetPosture) is logged once at Warning instead of being swallowed silently every check (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Read`).
- Added the shared in-game "What's new" popup (repo standing rule): after an update this changelog opens once; `/lazyfishsitter changelog` reopens it (files: `Plugin.cs`, `Configuration.cs` `LastSeenChangelogVersion`, `LazyFishSitter.csproj` compiles `src/Shared/LalaChangelog`).

v0.1.1.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added a second, independent seated signal: the game's own `EmoteController.GetPosture()` (`SittingOnGround` / `SittingInChair`), so detection works even if Mode reads Gathering while a line is cast; either signal counts as seated (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `ReadPosture`).

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- In-game "What's new" popup. - `/lazyfoodbuff changelog` (or `whatsnew`) reopens the release notes at any time.

- This is the pilot of a standing rule for every lalalazy plugin: the popup code is shared across plugins and each plugin embeds its own release notes at build time. New config field `Configuration.LastSeenChangelogVersion`; on the first build carrying the feature it records the running version silently and does not open.
- The popup never opens during combat, inside a duty, while zoning, or in a cutscene - it waits until the character is free.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Lazy Market Companion","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.8.15","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.
- Untried build: tested offline against a saved-configuration round trip (the plugin's offline test suite), not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.13 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's confirmation dialogs open now.** In 0.2.8.12, "Add all visible", "Remove all visible" and the panel's Enable Auto-Market switch each tried to show a confirmation dialog under a different name than the one they opened it with, so no dialog could ever appear and those controls did nothing when clicked. The names now match, and a regression test scans the panel's code so a button and its dialog cannot drift apart silently again.
- Correction to 0.2.8.12's notes: the panel's Enable Auto-Market switch asks for confirmation before turning Auto-Market on. That confirmation is the panel's own safety - the main window's switch has never had one, and 0.2.8.12's notes wrongly implied it did.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.12 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **A new Auto-Market panel window lists every marketable stack in your bags and whether it is on the Auto-Market list** - the same two states the bag dots mark (plus what a dot cannot show: entries whose tick is unticked, and the quick-exclude flag), as a table with quantities. Each row has quick Add/Remove, and entries expose the same stack-size, keep-in-bags and skip-routing edits as the main window's table. The panel covers your four bag containers, which is what Auto-Market's bags stock source draws from.
- **"Add all visible" / "Remove all visible" add or remove exactly the rows the filters currently show**, with the count on the button and a confirmation dialog before anything changes.
- **The panel carries the global Auto-Market knobs** in a collapsible section: master switch, markers, AutoRetainer, stock source, pricing, reserve slots, pinch behaviour, listing order, the value gate and auto-assign - the same controls as the Auto-Market tab, writing the same settings. What the main window does not expose is not exposed here either. The master switch keeps its confirmation on turning on and stays locked while a run is in progress.
- **Status filters, a name search, a category filter, and an optional count of unmarketable stacks** (hidden by default, like the dots' "no dot at all"). On-list rows keep the list's own order; everything else sorts by name. The panel never fetches prices, so the price-based listing orders are not applied here.
- **The panel docks beside the inventory window**: to its right when the screen has room, else to its left, else it floats at a position it remembers (clamped on screen, so it can never drift out of reach). It opens with the inventory, closes with it unless pinned, and `/lmc panel` toggles it any time. An inventory window that cannot be read is just the floating case - the panel always appears, and the plugin log's open line carries the dock mode, position, size, the inventory rectangle and scale it read, and the row counts.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.11 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Auto-Market marker dots are now drawn through a single full-screen drawing layer instead of one window per dot.** Every dot is painted directly onto one transparent overlay that covers the game's window - the same drawing path other screens in this plugin family use for game-anchored overlays - at exactly the same position as before. One window per dot could report itself healthy while nothing appeared on screen; that layer is gone entirely.
- **The markers log now checks each drawn dot against the inventory window's own position.** The game reports where the inventory window itself is (position, size, scale) in the same frame the dots are drawn; every measured dot is graded on-addon or OFF-ADDON against it, with its offset from the window's corner, so a placement mismatch names itself.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. v3.2.3.1 (2026-09-07)

- Removed the `/lazywtmath` command introduced in 3.2.3.0. It existed only to reopen the "What's new" popup, and this plugin's only interface is the probability readout inside the Wondrous Tails window itself.

v3.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After Lazy WT Math updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read.
- New command `/lazywtmath` reopens that popup. This plugin had no command at all before: the probabilities still appear inside the Wondrous Tails window itself, exactly as before, and nothing about how they are calculated has changed.
- The rebuild against current FFXIVClientStructs from 3.2.2.10 (which stopped the Wondrous Tails crash loop) is included.

v3.2.2.10 - 2026-09-05

- Fix for Helm thread t-plugerr-52f9741c16e8 (kanban t_a7838408). If the crash persists after updating, the next step is merging upstream MidoriKami/EzWondrousTails and its current KamiToolKit.

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","CanUnloadAsync":false,"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Changelog":"v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","IsTestingExclusive":false,"LoadPriority":0,"LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.4 (2026-10-22) [testing]
- **All 21 PvP rotations declare the upstream "Reborn" rotation type** (RotationSolverReborn 79f60d87c), upstream's tag for rotations written for the pre-Evercold job kits. Metadata only; rotations load and behave as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.3 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **All 21 PvP rotations declare game version 7.57**, and their source-code metadata points to the current rotation paths.
- **Paladin Guardian uses only the configured general-ability checks.** Duplicate attack-ability triggers that could bypass the HP and Hallowed Ground settings are removed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.2 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **When BossModReborn is unloaded, its timeline data (upcoming raidwides, tankbusters, knockbacks) is cleared once**, so proactive mitigation no longer acts on countdowns left over from before the unload.
- The last plugin lookup that could log an error on every call (the BossModReborn version lookup) reads the installed-plugin list instead.
- The BossModReborn check writes one log line when it first finds (or does not find) BossModReborn and one each time it is loaded or unloaded, never one per frame.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.1 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **BossModReborn integration was never detected, and it filled the log with errors.** The check for BossModReborn (and for WrathCombo) went through a lookup that cannot read BossModReborn's plugin object, so it reported the plugin as missing even while loaded, and wrote an error with a stack trace to the Dalamud log each time it was asked, once per frame while the settings window was open (over 11,000 lines in 35 minutes). The check now reads the list of installed plugins and quietly reports whether the plugin is loaded, so the BossModReborn timeline data is used when BossModReborn is running and the log stays clean.

v0.1.2.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **New settings window.** `/pvpsolver`, the plugin's settings button and Lazy Hub now open a new window with the settings that matter for PvP, in plain words with a help line under each. It has six tabs: Match (when PvP Solver turns itself on and off), Survival (Guard, Purify, Sprint and the defensives master switch), Targeting (who to attack, area attacks, burst, invulnerable enemies), My Job, Display and Advanced.
- **Settings can be changed in any zone.** Every setting, including each job's own options, can be edited anywhere and for any of the 21 jobs, not only for the played job inside a PvP zone. Only turning PvP Solver on still needs a PvP zone; its button says so. Job options need a character in the world.
- **Optional automatic defensives, all off by default.** Each is a "use when HP is below" setting with its own percentage, per job, in the My Job tab: Aquaveil (White Mage), Wreath of Ice (Black Mage), Tempera Coat (Pictomancer), Forte (Red Mage), Radiant Aegis (Summoner), Arcane Crest (Reaper), Snake Scales (Viper), The Blackest Night (Dark Knight), Holy Sheltron (Paladin), Bloodwhetting (Warrior), Curing Waltz (Dancer), and the PvP role actions Rampart (tanks) and Stoneskin II (healers), which can be used only while they are the selected role action. Recuperate keeps its existing rule (15,000 or more HP missing) and gains an optional second condition, an HP percentage. Default percentages run from 45 to 70.
- **Defensives master switch.** One switch in the Survival tab (on by default) turns all automatic defensives off at once. It also covers the six that were already automatic at a fixed HP: Heart of Corundum, Riddle of Earth, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui and Impalement, so turning it off stops those too.
- **Worst case of the defensives.** After one automatic defensive is used no other is used for 2.5 seconds, and none while a barrier, damage reduction or heal of the same kind from another turned-on defensive is still active, but with several turned on, more than one can still be used during one long stretch of low HP.
- **Six fixed HP thresholds are now settings with unchanged defaults.** Heart of Corundum (Gunbreaker) at or below 30%, Riddle of Earth (Monk) below 80%, Lady of Crowns and Microcosmos (Astrologian) below 60%, Meisui (Ninja) below 50% and Impalement (Dark Knight) below 60% behave exactly as before until changed. Each can be moved or turned off in the My Job tab.
- **Job options are stored per job.** Options were stored under the job being played, and the first time a job was used in a session its options shared one store, so same-named options (the Bloodbath and Smite thresholds of the six melee jobs) could carry over from one job to another. Each job's options are now stored under that job. Saved settings are kept.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The previous settings window is still available: Advanced tab, or `/pvpsolver advanced` (optionally followed by a tab name such as Actions).
- No saved setting is renamed or lost. The new settings use new keys that appear in the settings file only after they are changed.
- Checked offline only so far: the window layout, the automatic defensives with real targets and the job options of a job that is not being played have not yet been run in a match.

v0.1.1.5 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Targeting selection in PvP.** Entering the PvP state forced lowest-HP targeting, so the configured targeting list and the focus-fire (`PvPHighestPressure`) mode could not be selected. The configured list now applies; with default settings targeting is unchanged (lowest HP first).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.1.4 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Tank ability stall in PvP.** With several enemies in melee range and a tank's own mitigation on cooldown, the rotation stopped issuing every later ability until the situation ended. The defensive stage now hands over to the rest of the rotation in PvP.
- **Melee attack abilities considered at 5 yalms.** Melee jobs considered their attack abilities only with an enemy within 3 yalms although their weaponskills reach 5; in PvP the check now uses 5 yalms. Each ability still checks its own range.
- **Smite ignores Guard.** The target filter no longer excludes an enemy that has Guard when Smite is the action.
- **Sprint and Purify with no enemy nearby.** The list of actions allowed with no enemy within 40 yalms named the wrong actions; PvP Sprint and Purify are now allowed.
- **White Mage and Bard Guard, Recuperate and Elixir on the GCD path.** The emergency GCD step ended in the wrong base step and skipped them.
- **Scholar Chain Stratagem condition** now checks the enemy the action will actually target.
- **Viper Rattling Coil** no longer waits on Snake Scales, which the rotation never uses.
- **Gunbreaker.** The Blasting Zone 50% check reads the chosen target; the Heart of Corundum self-save now targets the Gunbreaker.
- **Paladin Guardian** respects the Hallowed Ground HP threshold and the 10-yalm limit.
- **Warden's Paean on allies (Bard) and Aquaveil on allies (White Mage).** The optional cleanse of other players could never find a target because it only counted afflictions the caster had applied; it now counts any affliction. Both options remain off by default.

    1.5.0.90: 
    * Updated to 7.4.
    * Some more changes coming soon but emergency maintenance started RIP
    
    1.5.0.82:
    * Reawakened Fangs Feature now also applies to Steel Maw.
    
    1.5.0.79:
    * Phlegma into Eukrasian Dyskrasia added.
    
    1.5.0.73:
    * Meisui/Tenri priority fixed and DWaD to Meisui added.
    * Monk's Draconic Leap feature now properly syncs below level 50 when you don't have a form.
    * Raise Hard Target Lockout Feature added.
    
    1.5.0.72:
    * Double Down features now account for its new cost.
    * New option for Royal Authority to Atonement where it will only activate if you are about to overwrite Sword Oath in your combo.
    * Empyreal Arrow will no longer turn into Pitch Perfect under any circumstances.
    
    1.5.0.71:
    * Updated for 7.1 compatibility.
    * Devilment to Starfall Dance feature removed as it is now vanilla.
    * Removed Jump to Mirage Dive due to it being vanilla, as I completely forgot to earlier.
    * Added an 'Only When Full' option to Sidewinder to Pitch Perfect.

    1.5.0.70:
    * Added Comet Overwrite Prevention feature. Or did I?
    * Removed Holy overcap features (it made no sense when you gain, not lose, DPS by letting it overcap).
    
    1.5.0.69 (Nice):
    * Sacrificium Feature added.
    * Despair to Flare Star added.
    * Dragon Kick to Forbidden Chakra added.
    
    1.5.0.67:
    * Blizzard 3 & 2 to Flare Star feature added.
    
    1.5.0.61:
    * Lucid Dreaming Reminders now have a configurable MP threshold, as well as a configurable cooldown remaining offset where they stop replacing the cooldown.
    
    1.5.0.60:
    * Combos to Saber Dance during Devilment feature added.
    * Some other stuff added to Dancer, too. Maybe.
    * Phlegma to Psyche added.
    
    1.5.0.59:
    * Isle Sprint feature added.
    
    1.5.0.53:
    * Reaving Steel added from regular XIVComboExpanded. Maybe something else, too? Tis a secret.
    * Hooking Hooksets and Chummy Cast added.
    
    1.5.0.51:
    * Chaotic Glide added.
    
    1.5.0.49:
    * Standard Step into Technical Step added.
    
    1.5.0.41:
    * Viper features added.  - **Added:** GIF picker (GIPHY search/trending, favourites, remembered searches), recent-DMs button with search, per-channel Server Rail colour, and ESC-clears-input toggle.

    - Automatically track your progress on objectives and tasks.

{"Author":"Cytraen, yomishino","Name":"Aether Compass","Punchline":"Compasses that detect and mark certain nearby objects/NPCs","Description":"This plugin detects certain objects/NPCs such as Aether Currents nearby and shows where they are by various ways, e.g. pointing to their locations on screen and notifying you in Chat.

Currently detects:
	- Aether Currents
	- Eureka Elementals (by apetih)
	- Mob Hunt Elite Marks
	- Gathering Points
	- [Experimental] Island Sanctuary Gathering Objects and Animals

{"Author":"SalvatoreDevelopment","Name":"AetherFM","Punchline":"Listen to radio in Eorzea!","Description":"In-game radio streaming for Final Fantasy XIV. Enter a stream URL and listen to your favorite radio! Features external plugin integration for Umbra widgets and other plugins via reflection.

Due to its reliance on the NAudio library, audio playback is not available on Linux or non-Windows versions of Dalamud.","Changelog":"This is a pretty big update. The directory now includes community events, Party Finder venue ads, notifications, and quite a few changes to how venues are displayed and filtered.

- Added a new Events tab. It shows FFXIV community events posted on Partake for the next two weeks, with filters for time, age rating, tags and location. You can also mark events with "I'm going" if you plan to attend.
- Party Finder venue ads collected by xivpf.com can now appear alongside events, as well as directly on the matching venue's page.
- Venues don't necessarily have to be listed on FFXIV Venues anymore. If a venue has an event on Partake or is currently advertising in Party Finder, it can still appear in the directory.
- Venue pages now show their upcoming events and any Party Finder ads that are currently active.
- Added optional notifications for favorite venues and events. The plugin can notify you when a favorite venue opens, when an event at a favorite venue starts, or 15 minutes before an event you've marked as going to. These notifications still work while the directory window is closed.
- Added "My data center" filtering. It follows the data center your current character is actually on, including after Data Center Travel. Location filters are remembered separately for each character.
- If you're standing on the plot of a listed venue, or you're already inside it, the top bar now tells you which venue you're at and gives you a quick way to mark it as visited.
- You can now hide venues you're not interested in. There's an undo option in the top bar, and hidden venues can always be found again with the Hidden filter.
- Venue descriptions now keep much more of their original formatting, including headings, bold and italic text, lists, links and images. Animated GIF, WebP and APNG images are supported too. Images in descriptions are only loaded over HTTPS and can be turned off in settings.
- Banners and images can optionally be enlarged by hovering over them. This is disabled by default.
- Locations outside the housing districts can now be opened on the in-game map.
- Settings have been moved into their own window and split into separate pages for appearance, images, events and notifications. There's also an About page with the changelog. You can use the directory's own theme or your Dalamud theme, change the UI size, and choose between a 12- or 24-hour clock.
- Schedule handling has been reworked. The directory now tries to show each venue's next actual opening in your local timezone instead of just displaying the raw weekly schedule. Monthly schedules, breaks, one-off openings and active venue notices are supported, and openings more than a week away show the date as well.
- Venue names and descriptions now show many more symbols and stylized letters; characters the game can't draw are replaced with plain letters instead of showing as boxes.
- Added a clearer error message for cases where FFXIV Venues refuses requests from your network or region.","TestingChangelog":"v1.2.0: IPC gates, Global search, Custom Stations, background playback, robustness.
- Formal IPC call gates (incl. ResumeLast, TogglePlayStop); non-throw policy; ordered events
- Global search (name/tag/language) and Custom Stations (add/list/remove)
- Favorites enhancements (names API), favorites always visible
- More stations: limit=10000, hide broken, clickcount order; wider stream validation (http/https,/stream, mp3/aac)
